moments.selftext: In 2001, actor Mark Ruffalo woke up in the middle of the night from a dream that he had a brain tumor. He had no symptoms at all. But the dream disturbed him enough to ask the doctor on his film set to check. The next day, a scan showed a tumor the size of a golf ball behind his left ear. The tumor was benign, but it was pressing on a facial nerve and had to be removed. Doctors warned him the surgery could leave him deaf, paralyzed on one side of his face, or both. There was one more problem. His wife was about to give birth to their first child. So Mark said nothing. He kept the diagnosis from his wife until a week after their son was born. When he finally told her, she thought he was joking. A few weeks later, surgeons removed the tumor. He woke up with the left side of his face frozen and no hearing in his left ear. His face took almost a year to recover. His hearing never did. Mark Ruffalo has been deaf in his left ear ever since.

moments.selftext: Claude has discovered a previously unknown enzyme system hidden in the DNA of bacteriophages. Beside the enzyme’s gene sits a long array of repeating DNA—a structure that looks somewhat similar to CRISPR. We don’t yet understand what this system does, but only a handful of known systems share its features, and all of them are able to cut, copy, and paste DNA. Historically, the discovery of such programmable systems has helped revolutionize medicine. CRISPR, for instance, is now the foundation of genetic medicines. But it will take much more work to learn what this system does, and whether it can be put to similar use. Read more:

moments.selftext: BREAKING: US M2 money supply jumped +$124.9 billion in August, to a record $23.34 trillion. This marks the 28th consecutive monthly increase, totaling +$2.61 trillion. YoY, M2 grew +5.7%, its largest YoY increase since June 2022. This marks a sharp acceleration from +2.0% YoY growth seen in August 2024. Meanwhile, since the 2020 pandemic, M2 money supply has surged +$7.85 trillion, equivalent to +$1.21 trillion on average per year, or +6.5% annualized growth. US money creation is picking up speed.
